profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap way, tagged telecom=data_center and named "Newrays Two LLC Mining," is located in Tennessee and is self-identified by name as a mining operation run under the entity Newrays Two LLC. The word "Mining" in an operator's own facility name, combined with a telecom=data_center tag, is a pattern seen repeatedly among cryptocurrency mining hosting sites that have been tagged in OpenStreetMap using the same general-purpose data-center key used for traditional colocation and cloud facilities, even though the underlying use case is materially different: racks of application-specific mining hardware drawing power for proof-of-work computation rather than general enterprise servers or cloud infrastructure serving external customers over a network uplink. Tennessee has attracted a number of such operations in recent years, often near favorable power pricing or surplus generation capacity. A Tennessee Secretary of State corporate registration for an entity named Newrays Two LLC would be the natural next primary source to confirm formation date and registered agent, and operator or trade-press coverage would help confirm hardware scale and site history, but neither could be retrieved this session due to search-tool quota limits. This entry should be read as a cryptocurrency mining hosting facility rather than a general-purpose data center, pending that fuller confirmation.

reading.body:
Newrays Two LLC Mining is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a data center in Henry County, Tennessee, but the facility name identifies it as a cryptocurrency mining operation rather than a general-purpose colocation or cloud infrastructure site. No published power specification, hardware count, or operator website could be retrieved to confirm the scale or current status of mining hardware on site. The classification depends on the self-descriptive name in the OpenStreetMap entry and remains unconfirmed by independent sources.

Tennessee hosts 24 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 publish power specifications totaling 12.13 MW. This facility does not appear among those four published figures, placing it outside the state's disclosed capacity despite its OSM presence.

Without a published megawatt figure, power contract details, or confirmed hardware inventory, Newrays Two LLC Mining cannot be evaluated as a constraint on AI scaling. Cryptocurrency mining and AI training are separate workloads with different economics and grid impacts. Confirmation of this site's current operation, power draw, and intended use would require corporate filings, operator contact, or on-site reporting.
